answer: Because the beacon weights are read from the voyage ledger at case open, the river audit records each vote and the weighting cannot be changed mid-case. Juror votes are weighted by stake up to 8 times the minimum, so a juror with real capital at risk outweighs a crowd of minimum-stake seats. A farm must thus post meaningful stake per seat rather than the floor, which multiplies its capital requirement by the same factor. That is 9 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
